title: SE Atelier: Integration Quickcards (draft)
body:
Purpose and audience:
- Short, slide-sized quickcards for systems engineers (SEs) and sellers to run fast technical discovery and handle integration/partner objections during pilots. Intended as an internal pocket-deck for pre-sales and partner onboarding.

Deck structure (speaker-note style):
1) Front: 30s framing
   - Slide title: SE Atelier — 30s integration framing
   - Speaker note: Two-sentence opener: Redwood Inference = predictable inference runtime + deployment modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private). For integration partners, highlight the three levers we control: latency SLOs, cost profile (batching/caching/quantization), and deployment options (VPC/private).
   - Micro-pitch (20s): "We give you a single API surface and operational controls so your engineering team doesn't have to re-architect when load grows or regulations tighten."

2) Discovery quickcard: environment + constraints
   - Slide title: What I need to know in 5 minutes
   - Bullets for SE to ask (read as checklist):
     • Workload type: chat, single-turn text, embeddings, or reranking?
     • Peak qps and typical sequence length distribution (p50/p95 tokens).
     • Latency SLO (p50/p95) — what breaks user experience?
     • Data residency & compliance: customer data stored? PII?
     • Deployment preference: hosted API vs dedicated pool vs private VPC?
     • Budget guardrails: $/M tokens, or reservations?
   - Note: capture these answers verbatim in pilot intake template (link to JIRA/Confluence).

3) Typical objections + micro-responses (engineer-first):
   - Objection: "We need on-prem for compliance."
     • Quick response: "We support Private (VPC/on-prem) with optional air-gapped rollout. Common pattern: start hosted for speed, export deployment manifest, then replicate infra on-prem for sensitive traffic."
     • Tech hook: mention KMS/HSM integration and audit logs.
   - Objection: "Latency is non-deterministic at scale."
     • Quick response: "Dedicated reservation with pinned GPU pools and autoscale policies gives stable p95s; we can run a smoke load with production-like sequences and share histogram traces."
     • Tech hook: provide tracing sample (we attach a trace link after a test run).
   - Objection: "How do we control costs for high-volume embeddings?"
     • Quick response: "Batching + prefix caching + embedding caching reduce per-embedding amortized cost. We’ll propose a quantization profile and a warm KV cache strategy for cold-start-heavy flows."

4) Pilot checklist (operational):
   - Slide title: Pilot in 6 steps (30–90 day)
   - Steps with quick signals for success:
     1) Kickoff + discovery (one pager + sample payloads) — deliver sample workload attachment to GTM JIRA ticket.
     2) Smoke tests (dev to hosted) — validate correctness & run 1k-5k tokens test to collect latency/cost baseline.
     3) Throughput run (dedicated if needed) — run p99 stress test at target qps.
     4) Integrate auth & keys (rotate policy) — ensure KMS integration for private.
     5) Observability check — enable per-route token traces, cost dashboards, and alerting.
     6) Canary & rollback plan — define fallback model variants and canary threshold.
   - Acceptance criteria (short): accuracy within agreed metric window, latency p95 within target, cost per 1k inference under agreed ceiling, no security blockers.

5) Fallback patterns (mini cheat-sheet):
   - Title: Fallback matrix (keep app live)
   - Patterns:
     • Model fallback: full-precision -> quantized -> CPU-optimized smaller model.
     • Route fallback: region A -> region B -> Dedicated reserve.
     • Degraded mode: strip non-critical augmentations (suggestions, contextual expansions) to preserve latency.
   - Implementation snippet (verbal): configure routing policy with priority list + exponential backoff for retries, alert on >1% fallback rate for 10m.

6) Integration snippets (one-liners for SE to copy):
   - API quickcall (pseudo): POST /v1/infer { model: "redwood-chat-medium", input: "...", route_policy: "primary,dedicated,fallback" }
   - Canary test prompt (example): "Given this short user query, return top-3 concise responses and a confidence score."
   - Observability query (console): show token-cost by route, latency histogram p50/p95, and top error types.

7) Sample email templates (3 lines each)
   - Kickoff to partner engineer:
     Subject: Redwood pilot kickoff — quick steps
     Body: "Hi <name>, thanks again. Attached sample payloads + our smoke test plan. Proposed times for 1h kickoff this week: Tue 10–11 or Wed 2–3. — Maya"
   - Post-smoke summary to customer:
     Subject: Smoke test results + next steps
     Body: "Smoke passed: p95 latency X ms, embedding cost Y/token. Recommend dedicated pilot for throughput next. See attached run artifacts. — Maya"

8) Escalation play (when pilot hits blockers)
   - Slide title: Escalation path — who to loop in
   - Quick map: AE -> SE -> Solutions Eng -> SRE oncall -> Product PM if architectural gap. Include suggested Slack escalation channel names in notes.
   - When to escalate: repeated p95 misses after tuning, reproducible correctness mismatch vs baseline, legal/regulatory redline on storage.

9) Open questions & next small experiments
   - Should we standardize a lightweight pilot bundle (payload + cost cap + success gates)?
   - Experiment idea: 2-week cold-start cache experiment to quantify warmup benefit for chat with long contexts.
   - Action items: Ruben to draft pilot bundle, Priya to enumerate required audit evidence for private deployments.

Appendix (quick references):
   - Common model tiers and cost guidance (one-line each): tiny => low-latency low-capacity; medium => balanced; large => high-accuracy, higher cost.
   - Link placeholders: Confluence intake, JIRA pilot board, GitHub examples (already linked at top).

Tone notes for SEs and sellers: keep it crisp, engineer-first, avoid marketing fluff. Use these cards as copy-paste snippets in Slack or emails.

Unresolved bits for next iteration:
   - Add real sample traces and synthetic workloads (need infra run).
   - Create slide images for fallback-flow diagram.
   - Gather 3 partner case snapshots (anonymized) to show outcomes.

Document provenance and usage: internal draft for SE bootcamp and partner onboarding; intended to iterate after 2 live pilots.
